The file has two candidates: `countPrimes` (trial division up to n for each n) and `dedupe` (linear `includes` inside a loop). I'll time each one without modifying the file.
`countPrimes` takes most of the time. In an isolated timing run it took about 634 ms, versus about 147 ms for `dedupe`, so roughly 80% of the script's runtime.

It is slow because `isPrime` tests every divisor from 2 up to n-1 with no early stop at √n, so the total work across all n below 60,000 is about 1.8 billion modulo operations. `dedupe` is quadratic too, but its input is small enough (30,000 values) that it costs far less. I did not change any files.
